facts.intro: A rope runs over a round wheel attached to a fixed axle, forming a simple pulley system.
facts.reveal: When you pull the free end of the rope, the wheel turns around its pin.
facts.step1: The turning wheel lifts the attached weight, which is a sack of laundry hanging on the other side.
facts.step2: As the weight rises, the rope shortens on the side attached to the weight and lengthens on the side you hold.
facts.step3: The spring‑loaded tension in the rope keeps the wheel snug against the pin, preventing slip.
facts.step4: Releasing the rope lets the weight’s gravity pull it back down, turning the wheel in reverse.
facts.hold: If you hold the rope steady, the weight stays suspended, demonstrating a balanced load.
facts.payoff: The pulley lets a small hand force lift a heavier load, just like a window blind or well bucket.
